t: 二度あることは三度ある
r: にどあることはさんどある
mean: what has happened twice is likely to happen a third time
lit: what happens twice will happen three times

r: そなえあればうれいなし
mean: if you are prepared, you have nothing to worry about

In the chapter in which the minister Fu Yue advises King Wu Ding of Shang, he says that every undertaking needs its preparation, and that where there is preparation there is nothing to fear. Its four-character phrase, read the Japanese way, became this proverb.
